# BAD-092 — npm run web:local leaves the local collab flag on, which fails the server suite's flag_off case

## Brief
scripts/web-local.js runs 'update private.feature_flags set default_value = true where key = collab' and never puts it back, so any later run of test/server/functions.test.mjs against the same stack fails. The suite's own comment at :2517 says the flag is seeded OFF on a fresh stack and guards against a leaked targeting RULE dropped in a finally -- but nothing guards against default_value itself having been flipped, which is the one thing the web dev loop does on purpose. Two documented tools on one shared stack that silently break each other.

Evidence: Hit it in this worktree today. Ran 'npm run web:local' for BAD-080's end-to-end, then npm test with functions served: one failure, 'expected { error: flag_off, code: flag_off }, actual { error: not_a_member, code: not_a_member }' at test/server/functions.test.mjs:2744 -- the flag being on lets the request past the wall and into the membership check. Verified the cause directly: 'select key, default_value from private.feature_flags' reads collab|t, while migration 0015_collab_flag.sql:13 seeds it false. Same failure will greet anyone who runs the server suite on this machine until someone sets it back; I was refused permission to write to the shared DB, so it is still on as I finish. Options: have web-local.js restore the prior value on exit, have the suite assert/reset default_value the way it already drops its rule, or say plainly in server/README.md that the two cannot share a stack.
